theory.intro: A simple interest graph shows interest earned over time. Because the same interest is earned each period, the interest-time graph is a **straight line through the origin**, and its gradient represents the annual interest.
facts: $I = Prn$ produces a straight-line graph passing through $(0, 0)$ when interest is plotted against time.
The gradient of the line equals the annual interest earned, $Pr$.
On the same axes, a steeper line has a larger annual interest amount $Pr$. It indicates a higher rate when the principals are equal, or a larger principal when the rates are equal.
A graph of total investment value against time has a vertical intercept at $(0, P)$.
To find interest at time $t$, read vertically to the line then across to the vertical axis.
steps: Identify whether the vertical axis represents interest $I$ or total value $A$, and read both axis scales. Time here is in years and the rate is per annum.
For a given time, read up to the line and across to the vertical axis. For a given interest or balance, read across to the line and down to the time axis.

Find the annual interest from the increase in interest or balance divided by the time interval. On a balance graph, read the initial principal at time zero, or subtract the interest earned from a later balance.

Use annual interest $=Pr$ to find an unknown rate or principal. Write rates as decimals for calculations and multiply a decimal rate by $100$ for a percentage. Compare annual interest amounts to find an interest difference over time, or divide the required difference by the annual difference to find time.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Read up from $3$ years, then across: $I=\$495$.
(b) Read across from $\$660$, then down: $4$ years.
(c) Annual interest $=495\div3=\$165$.
$r=165\div3200=0.0515625$.
Annual rate $\approx5.16\%$.

(a) At time zero, $P=\$4300$. The vertical scale starts at $\$4000$, not zero.
(b) $I=A-P=5275-4300=\$975$.
(c) Annual interest $=(5275-4690)\div(5-2)$

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Investment A has $\$3500$ at $4.8\%$ p.a.; B has $\$2400$ at $7\%$ p.a. Explain why their interest-time lines coincide on the same axes.
(b) C has $\$4000$ at $4.8\%$ p.a. Is its interest line steeper than A?
(c) Another interest line earns $\$207$ each year at $4.5\%$ p.a. Find its principal.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) A annual interest $=3500\times0.048=\$168$.
B annual interest $=2400\times0.07=\$168$.
Both start at zero interest and increase by the same amount each year.
(b) C annual interest $=4000\times0.048=\$192$, greater than $\$168$, so C is steeper. Equal rates do not mean equal annual amounts when principals differ.
(c) $P=207\div0.045=\$4600$.

workedExamples.question_text:
X earns simple interest on $\$7200$ at $3.5\%$ p.a.; Y earns simple interest on $\$4800$ at $6.75\%$ p.a.
(a) Find how much more interest Y earns after $7$ years.
(b) How long until Y has earned $\$1080$ more interest than X?
workedExamples.solution_text:
X annual interest $=7200\times0.035=\$252$.
Y annual interest $=4800\times0.0675=\$324$.
Annual difference $=324-252=\$72$.
(a) Difference after $7$ years $=72\times7=\$504$.
(b) Time $=1080\div72=15$ years.

Investment $X$ has $P = \$10\,000$ at $3.5\%$ p.a. simple interest.
Investment $Y$ has $P = \$6000$ at $7\%$ p.a. simple interest.
After how many years will Investment $Y$ have earned $\$1400$ more total interest than Investment $X$?

Two investments earn simple interest at $4.5\%$ p.a.
On an interest graph, their lines have equations $I = 180t$ and $I = 270t$.
Calculate the principal invested in each account.
